subject: Re: Kestrel AI - rate protections, MFN, and CPI cap negotiation
messages:
From: Olivia Park <olivia.park@kestrelai.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@kestrelai.com>
Date: 2026-06-12T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Kestrel request: price protections + commit tiers

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the latency profile looked great. Procurement asked me to follow up with a concise summary of our asks so they can circulate internally. High-level: we want to move to a hosted API consumption model but need commercial protections to proceed. Could you confirm Redwood's stance on the following?

- Price lock: 12 months guaranteed unit price for the committed tiers (no increases during the lock period).
- MFN (most favored nation): Kestrel requests MFN against any customer with equal or lower commitment level for the same model family.
- CPI cap: tying price changes to CPI, capped at 2.5% annually (we're ok with an annual True-Up).
- Commit tiers: preference for a 12 month committed $/month spend (we'll share expected volume in attachment).

I've attached our usage forecast (Kestrel_Metrics.xlsx). We're looking to align economics quickly — procurement wants a redlined term sheet this week if possible.

Thanks,
Olivia Park
Head of Platform Partnerships
Kestrel AI

---
Attachment: Kestrel_Metrics.xlsx (excel)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Park <olivia.park@kestrelai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-12T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Kestrel request: price protections + commit tiers

Olivia — thanks for the clear list and the forecast. Appreciated. Quick summary of what we can do and what we need to scope with legal/procurement:

1) Price lock: We can offer a 12-month price lock for committed tiers on hosted API usage provided: the customer signs a 12-month commit (min $X/month; see tier table below), and usage stays within agreed tolerance bands. Hardware pass-through costs (rare) and extraordinary taxes are excluded.

2) MFN: We are open to a limited MFN for identical commitment levels and service scope. We cannot provide broad MFN across all contracts (varied customer-specific SLAs, add-ons). MFN will be scoped to: model family, term length, and tiered committed spend.

3) CPI cap: We can accept an annual increase cap tied to US CPI, capped at 3.0% (Redwood proposes 3% to allow runway). Alternatively, fixed 12-month lock with no CPI adjustments in year 1 and then CPI-based adjustments thereafter — open to Kestrel preference.

4) Commit tiers (hosted usage): we typically propose three commit bands:
   - Band A: $25k/month commit — baseline pricing P_base (e.g., $0.0006 per token) with 10% effective discount off list for the committed volume.
   - Band B: $75k/month commit — P_mid (approx $0.00048 per token) with 18% discount and priority burst capacity.
   - Band C: $200k/month commit — P_enterprise (approx $0.00036 per token) with 28% discount, SLA add-ons included.

All tiers allow overage billing at the committed tier rate for a short grace period and then revert to on-demand price if sustained. We can convert committed dollars to token buckets during contract drafting.

Next steps: I'll have Marissa draft a commercial term-sheet (v1) and circulate. For MFN / CPI precise language we'll need a brief call with procurement and legal (15–30m). Does Thursday 6/17 at 10am PT work for you?

I'll attach a short pricing summary (pdf) for internal reference.

Thanks —
Karthik Iyer
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

---
Attachment: redwood_proposed_pricing_summary.pdf (pdf)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Park <olivia.park@kestrelai.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@kestrelai.com>
Date: 2026-06-14T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Draft term sheet + clarifications on MFN and CPI language

Looping in a draft term sheet (attached) and a couple clarifications from legal so procurement has context:

- MFN: draft limits MFN applicability to commercial terms for the exact same model family and committed spend band. It excludes bespoke add-ons (e.g., private deployment fee, dedicated reserved GPUs).

- CPI clause: draft provides two options — (A) 12 months fixed price (no CPI for year 1) then CPI-based true-up capped at 3% annually thereafter; or (B) immediate CPI-linked adjustments capped at 2.5% (your ask). Please mark the preferred option in the term sheet.

- Price lock operational detail: we require monthly reporting against committed buckets; small month-to-month variance +/-15% is tolerated. Sustained overage (>3 consecutive months above committed) will trigger rate re-evaluation.

- Overage handling: short bursts billed at committed tier price for the first 30 days in a rolling 12-month period, then on-demand thereafter.

If Kestrel wants MFN to include credits/one-time promotions, we will need to carve out those transient items. Happy to discuss on the call Karthik proposed.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Head of Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

---
Attachment: term_sheet_draft_v1.docx (docx)
From: Olivia Park <olivia.park@kestrelai.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@kestrelai.com>
Date: 2026-06-15T15:09:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Draft term sheet + clarifications on MFN and CPI language

Marissa / Karthik — thank you for the quick turnaround and the detailed draft. Procurement reviewed and here's where we stand:

- CPI cap: Kestrel prefers option B (immediate CPI adjustments, capped at 2.5%). If you can accept 2.5% we'll remove that as an internal blocker.
- MFN: we can accept the limit to identical model family and commitment band. We do want MFN to include any publicly advertised list price reductions during the term (i.e., if you lower list price for that model family, Kestrel gets the lower list).
- Price lock: Kestrel is comfortable with the monthly reporting requirement and +/-15% tolerance. For overage handling we prefer a 45 day grace for bursts instead of 30.

Action items for Redwood: please update the term sheet with (1) CPI cap at 2.5% (if acceptable), (2) MFN clause to include publicly advertised list changes, and (3) 45 day burst grace. If that's acceptable we'll route to our legal for redlines and can sign a term sheet to kick off procurement.

Best,
Olivia Park
Head of Platform Partnerships
Kestrel AI
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Park <olivia.park@kestrelai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-18T16:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Draft term sheet + clarifications on MFN and CPI language

Olivia — appreciate the clear asks. We can accept the revised commercial points with the following small clarifications:

- CPI cap: Redwood will accept 2.5% cap (as requested) tied to US CPI (all-items) annual change.
- MFN: we'll include publicly advertised list price reductions in the MFN scope, but carve out short-term promotional credits and partner channel-specific rebates (we'll list those).
- Burst grace: we'll extend to 45 days as requested, measured on a rolling 12-month basis.

We'll update term_sheet_draft_v1 with these changes and send v2 for your legal's redline. If that looks good, let's confirm Thursday 6/24 at 10am PT for a final commercial call and to agree on signature authority.

I also copied Sean on this note — Sean, can you confirm that Kestrel's expected peak Q4 burst (per their forecast) is within our available capacity for priority bursts under Band B?

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
